lawp.circuits.basics.what-is-a-loop: See how a closed path lets a lamp light.
lawp.circuits.basics.brighter-lamp: Predict what will happen, then change the circuit so the lamp shines brighter.
lawp.circuits.basics.why-the-limit: Learn why too much current is a problem, and what a safe limit is for.
lawp.circuits.basics.transfer-fuse: Use the same current idea in a new story about a fuse.
lawp.circuits.basics.keep-your-circuit: Keep the circuit you built and take it with you.

lawp.python.foundations.names-and-values: A name holds a value you can use again later.
lawp.python.foundations.types-you-can-see: Numbers, text, and true or false are different kinds of value.
lawp.python.foundations.walk-the-fox: Call a step so the fox walks one cell on the grid.
lawp.python.foundations.compare-is-not-assign: Asking whether two things are equal is not the same as giving a name a value.
lawp.python.foundations.if-this-then-that: A decision picks one path when a check is true.
lawp.python.foundations.say-it-once: Write a message once and reuse it instead of repeating yourself.
lawp.python.foundations.greeting-bot: Build a small greeting you can keep and run again.

lawp.react.foundations.function-returns-ui: A component is a function that returns what should appear on the page.
lawp.react.foundations.props-flow-in: Values flow into a component from the outside.
lawp.react.foundations.click-changes-state: A click replaces what the screen remembers, then it redraws.
lawp.react.foundations.list-needs-key: Each item in a list needs a stable key so updates stay honest.
lawp.react.foundations.filter-the-list: Show only the items that match what the learner asked for.
lawp.react.foundations.keep-the-app: Keep the list you built and take it with you.

lawp.learning.questions.check-kinds: Try every way a question can look, then see how answering works.
lawp.learning.questions.check-mcq: Pick the one choice that is right.
lawp.learning.questions.check-multi: Check every box that is true. Missing one fails.
lawp.learning.questions.check-odd: Find the item that does not belong with the others.
lawp.learning.questions.check-tf: Decide whether a closed fact is true or false.
lawp.learning.questions.check-image: Tap the picture that matches the prompt.
lawp.learning.questions.check-short: Type a short word. Close spellings still pass.
lawp.learning.questions.check-select: Choose the missing word from a menu in the sentence.
lawp.learning.questions.check-numeric: Enter the number, with a unit if the question has one.
lawp.learning.questions.check-fix: Edit the broken sentence until it is right.
lawp.learning.questions.check-cloze: Fill each blank from a short list of words.
lawp.learning.questions.check-bank: Drag words from a shared pile into the blanks.
lawp.learning.questions.check-match: Connect each item on the left to its pair on the right.
lawp.learning.questions.check-order: Put the steps in the order they should happen.
lawp.learning.questions.check-place: Drag each piece onto the right spot on a diagram.
lawp.learning.questions.check-hotspot: Tap the region on the picture that answers the question.
lawp.learning.questions.check-gorder: Tap the spots on the picture in the order they should happen.
lawp.learning.questions.check-bins: Sort the cards into buckets. Leftovers can stay out.
lawp.learning.questions.check-venn: Place each item in the left set, the right set, both, or neither.
lawp.learning.questions.check-hottext: Tap the word in the passage that is wrong or that proves the claim.
lawp.learning.questions.check-table: Choose an answer for every row, using the same choices.
lawp.learning.questions.check-tier: Pick an answer, then pick the reason that matches it.
lawp.learning.questions.check-slider: Estimate a value on a range. Close enough still passes.
lawp.learning.questions.check-numberline: Pin the number on the line.
lawp.learning.questions.check-listen: Play the clip, then pick what you heard.

lawp.javascript.foundations.js-placement: A short quiz about what you already expect JavaScript to do. Wrong answers do not lock you out.
lawp.javascript.foundations.values-and-typeof: Every value has a kind: number, text, or true and false. You need this before any list.
lawp.javascript.foundations.names-let-const: A name is a box for a value. Some boxes you can refill. Some you cannot rebind.
lawp.javascript.foundations.strings-and-templates: Text can be a plain string or a template that fills in values.
lawp.javascript.foundations.numbers-and-nan: Some calculations have no numeric answer. Spot NaN and do not treat it as zero.
lawp.javascript.foundations.triple-equals: Strict equality compares value and kind. Loose equality will surprise you.
lawp.javascript.foundations.truth-and-if: Some values act as no in a decision. An empty list is still a list.
lawp.javascript.foundations.short-circuit: And, or, and nullish stop as soon as they know the answer. Zero is a real reading.
lawp.javascript.foundations.transfer-classify-signal: Use kinds of values to label a signal in a new story.
lawp.javascript.foundations.functions-call: Name a function and pass values in to run it. Nothing runs until you call it.
lawp.javascript.foundations.beacon-call: Walk the fox onto the beacon by calling a move, one cell at a time.
lawp.javascript.foundations.return-not-print: Showing a value is not the same as handing it back to the caller.
lawp.javascript.foundations.parameters-and-defaults: A function can take values in. Missing ones can have a fallback.
lawp.javascript.foundations.loops-for: A counted loop writes a path, one step per turn.
lawp.javascript.foundations.loops-while-break: Keep going while a condition is true. Stop when you have a reason.
lawp.javascript.foundations.keyed-beacon: Collect every token, then stand on the beacon facing the right way.
lawp.javascript.foundations.debug-off-by-one-path: The walk is one cell short. Find the off-by-one and fix it.
lawp.javascript.foundations.arrays-index: Length is how many items. Index is the place of one item.
lawp.javascript.foundations.arrays-map: Make a new list from an old one. The original stays put.
lawp.javascript.foundations.arrays-filter-find: Keep the items that match, or find the first one that does.
lawp.javascript.foundations.arrays-reduce-once: Fold a list into one value, and be able to say why.
lawp.javascript.foundations.objects-props: A record holds named fields you can read and change.
lawp.javascript.foundations.set-and-map: A set keeps each value once. A map stores a value under a key you choose.
lawp.javascript.foundations.reference-vs-copy: Two names can point at the same object. A copy is a new one.
lawp.javascript.foundations.destructure-spread: Pull fields out of a record, or copy them into a new one.
lawp.javascript.foundations.json-roundtrip: Turn a record into text and back again without losing the shape.
lawp.javascript.foundations.signal-log: Build a small log of signals you can keep working on.
lawp.javascript.foundations.scope-and-tdz: A name is only alive in its block. Using it too early is a fault.
lawp.javascript.foundations.closures-radio: A function can remember values from the place it was created.
lawp.javascript.foundations.callbacks-as-commands: A table of functions is a set of commands you can call by name.
lawp.javascript.foundations.arrow-vs-function: Two ways to write a function. They are not the same about this.
lawp.javascript.foundations.higher-order-route: Pass a function into another function so the walk can change.
lawp.javascript.foundations.stale-closure-debug: The last direction keeps winning. Find why the old value stuck.
lawp.javascript.foundations.transfer-command-table: Build a new maze from a table of commands.
lawp.javascript.foundations.throw-and-catch: Throw a problem, catch it, and keep walking.
lawp.javascript.foundations.finally-and-rethrow: Work that must run after a try, even when you throw again.
lawp.javascript.foundations.custom-errors: Make your own error type so the catch can tell stories apart.
lawp.javascript.foundations.debug-read-the-stack: Read the stack to see which call failed and why.
lawp.javascript.foundations.coercion-to-primitive: An object can be asked to become a simple value. Know what it answers.
lawp.javascript.foundations.prototypes-chain: A missing field is looked up on the object behind this one.
lawp.javascript.foundations.new-and-create: Two ways to make an object that shares a prototype.
lawp.javascript.foundations.classes-syntax: Class syntax is sugar over the same prototype story.
lawp.javascript.foundations.this-call-apply-bind: This is who the function is talking about, not where it was written.
lawp.javascript.foundations.descriptors-get-set: A field can run code when you read or write it.
lawp.javascript.foundations.symbols: A unique key that will not clash with ordinary names.
lawp.javascript.foundations.weak-collections: Notes that do not keep an object alive after you let it go.
lawp.javascript.foundations.iterators-for-of: A custom list of directions you can walk with a for-of loop.
lawp.javascript.foundations.generators: A function that yields the next step when you ask.
lawp.javascript.foundations.proxies-reflect: Intercept one read or write and decide what it means.
lawp.javascript.foundations.transfer-model-a-part: Model a part as an object with the same rules you just learned.
lawp.javascript.foundations.stack-vs-heap: Calls sit on a stack. Objects live on the heap until nothing points at them.
lawp.javascript.foundations.macrotasks-timeout: A timeout waits until the current work is done, then it runs.
lawp.javascript.foundations.microtasks-then: A then callback runs before the next timeout. They are not the same tray.
lawp.javascript.foundations.promises-states: A promise is pending, kept, or broken. It does not change again.
lawp.javascript.foundations.async-await: Await pauses this function until a promise settles, then continues.
lawp.javascript.foundations.async-errors: A rejected await belongs in try and catch, like a throw.
lawp.javascript.foundations.parallel-vs-sequence: Wait for many promises together, or one after another on purpose.
lawp.javascript.foundations.async-iterators: Walk a stream of steps as each one arrives.
lawp.javascript.foundations.transfer-beacon-dispatch: Time a walk on the grid using what you just learned about waiting.
lawp.javascript.foundations.debug-forgotten-await: The walk finishes too soon. Find the missing wait.
lawp.javascript.foundations.tree-not-string: The page is a tree of nodes, not a pile of text.
lawp.javascript.foundations.query-and-update: Find a node, then change the text it shows.
lawp.javascript.foundations.create-and-remove: Make a node, put it in the tree, or take it out.
lawp.javascript.foundations.events-bubble: A click rises through the tree unless you stop it.
lawp.javascript.foundations.delegation: One listener on a parent can handle many children.
lawp.javascript.foundations.forms-and-input: Read what the learner typed as they type it.
lawp.javascript.foundations.prevent-default: Stop the form from leaving the page, then copy the typed words onto the board.
lawp.javascript.foundations.a11y-name-and-role: A control needs a name and a role a screen reader can use.
lawp.javascript.foundations.xss-text-vs-html: Put plain words in as text. Do not feed them as markup.
lawp.javascript.foundations.transfer-filter-list-ui: Filter a list on a real page using the same tree ideas.
lawp.javascript.foundations.creation-signal-board: Keep a signal board on the page and take it with you.
lawp.javascript.foundations.http-as-messages: A request and a response are messages, not magic.
lawp.javascript.foundations.method-and-headers: A request has a method and labels. Those labels tell the other side how to read the body.
lawp.javascript.foundations.fetch-ok-and-fail: A missing page is still a response. Only a broken network throws.
lawp.javascript.foundations.json-body: Reading a body as data can fail. Handle the bad text.
lawp.javascript.foundations.abort-and-timeout: Cancel a request on purpose when you have waited long enough.
lawp.javascript.foundations.cors-mental-model: The browser decides whether page code may read another origin.
lawp.javascript.foundations.transfer-library-search: Search a fixture of records the way a library search would.
lawp.javascript.foundations.process-argv-env: A program can read the words you typed and the environment around it.
lawp.javascript.foundations.fs-read-write: Read and write a text file on disk.
lawp.javascript.foundations.paths-and-encoding: Join path parts safely. Do not walk above the folder you meant.
lawp.javascript.foundations.buffers-vs-strings: Bytes are not the same as text. Decode them on purpose.
lawp.javascript.foundations.streams-idea: Read a log in chunks instead of all at once.
lawp.javascript.foundations.cjs-vs-esm-node: Two module styles. Know which file is which.
lawp.javascript.foundations.error-first-and-promises: Older file calls pass an error first. Newer ones return a promise.
lawp.javascript.foundations.transfer-clean-a-log: Clean a names log using files and the process.
lawp.javascript.foundations.creation-log-scrubber: Keep a log scrubber you can run again.
lawp.javascript.foundations.assert-and-aaa: Arrange the world, act, then assert what must be true.
lawp.javascript.foundations.fixtures-and-hidden-tests: Hidden tests use fixtures. Your file is the thing they call.
lawp.javascript.foundations.mocking-time-and-fs: Fake the clock and the disk so a test does not wait or write for real.
lawp.javascript.foundations.why-bundlers: A bundler packs modules for the page. Know why that step exists.
lawp.javascript.foundations.modules-esm-files: Export a walker from one file and import it in another.
lawp.javascript.foundations.ast-and-lint: A linter reads the shape of the code, not only the text.
lawp.javascript.foundations.proto-pollution: Do not let outside data write into the shared object behind every record.
lawp.javascript.foundations.measure-then-change: Measure first. Change one thing. Measure again.
lawp.javascript.foundations.jsdoc-contracts: A short comment can be a checklist of what a function owes.
lawp.javascript.foundations.transfer-test-the-fox: Write tests for a walk so a later change cannot silently break it.
lawp.javascript.foundations.capstone-signal-ops: Put the path together: walk, records, the page, and tests.
lawp.javascript.foundations.optional-chaining: Reach through a record that may be missing without crashing. The question mark dot stops at the first gap, and it is not a default.
lawp.javascript.foundations.switch-dispatch: One command name picks between many branches. Grouped labels share a body on purpose, and a missing stop runs the next branch by accident.
lawp.javascript.foundations.object-key-iteration: Walk a record by its own keys, its values, or both. The older loop also hands you inherited keys.
lawp.javascript.foundations.promise-combinators: Waiting for a group is three questions. Require every part, report what each part did, or take whichever answer lands first.
lawp.javascript.foundations.regex-lines: A pattern pulls fields out of a log line and squeezes the spacing. Without the global flag it fixes only the first match.
